candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort → Nutrition and Oral Hydration: provide nutrition-related care and education based on disease state, treatment modality, laboratory findings, and individualized client needs.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — protein needs after transition to maintenance hemodialysis
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that dietary protein requirements change when a metabolically stable adult begins maintenance hemodialysis and that the overall dialysis diet must be individualized rather than simply continuing a predialysis low-protein prescription.

options.A: Protein needs change after maintenance dialysis begins; the renal dietitian should reassess intake because stable hemodialysis clients generally require more dietary protein than many nondialysis CKD clients, while potassium, phosphorus, sodium, and fluid advice remains individualized.
options.B: Continue the same low-protein restriction indefinitely because maintenance hemodialysis never changes protein requirements.
options.C: Avoid nearly all protein after dialysis begins because dietary protein interferes with urea removal and makes hemodialysis ineffective.
options.D: Once hemodialysis starts, diet no longer needs to consider nutrition status, laboratory findings, residual urine output, or treatment schedule.

candidate.rationale: The current KDOQI Nutrition in CKD guideline distinguishes protein recommendations before and after maintenance dialysis. In metabolically stable adults with CKD 5D on maintenance hemodialysis, KDOQI recommends a dietary protein intake of 1.0–1.2 g/kg body weight per day to maintain stable nutritional status, whereas lower protein prescriptions may be used under close supervision in selected nondialysis CKD 3–5 populations. Current NKF hemodialysis nutrition guidance also emphasizes that potassium, phosphorus, sodium, fluid, calories, and other dietary needs must be individualized using laboratory results, residual urine output, treatment schedule, and nutrition status. Therefore, A is correct. B and C inappropriately continue or intensify protein restriction after dialysis starts, and D rejects individualized nutrition assessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports higher protein requirements in stable maintenance hemodialysis than many nondialysis CKD protein-restriction plans and supports individualized dialysis nutrition rather than a universal fixed diet.
candidate.source_document_title: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update; Hemodialysis and Your Diet
